c29_pro_thinking_003.label: Availability Heuristic and Perceived Violence
c29_pro_thinking_003.description: The availability heuristic is when people estimate the frequency of an event by how easily examples come to mind, leading to biases like overestimating violence because of media exposure.
coverage_criteria: Student can explain the availability heuristic and describe how it can distort perceptions of violence rates.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The source introduces the availability heuristic at 01:21-01:44, using the example of perceived rising violence versus actual data showing a decline.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: This concept is a key heuristic that can be tested by asking the student to identify it or apply it to another scenario.

c29_pro_thinking_004.label: Representativeness Heuristic and Medical Test Fallacy
c29_pro_thinking_004.description: The representativeness heuristic is when people assume an individual case is more representative than it truly is, often ignoring base rates, as seen when physicians overestimate disease likelihood after a positive test.
coverage_criteria: Student can define the representativeness heuristic and explain why a positive test for a rare disease does not guarantee having the disease.

extraction_reason.source_grounded_rationale: The source details the representativeness heuristic from 01:49-02:53 with a medical test example, showing that people ignore base rates and false positive rates.
extraction_reason.granularity_rationale: This is a specific heuristic that can be checked with a problem-solving question or definition.
